archetype.name: Dual-Threat (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A 12-year veteran QB2 whose value has always come from his legs and a quick, accurate short game, rather than from pushing the ball downfield or carrying an offense for long stretches.

report.headline: Steady relief work built on short throws, now shelved by an MCL sprain
report.take:
Mariota is what Washington pays him to be: a backup who can run the offense without wrecking it. His three appearances add up to 0.21 EPA per dropback (13th of 42), no interceptions and no fumbles. The career line shows the type. In every season he played real volume he ranked in the top nine at the position in rushing yards, with middling CPOE and too many interceptions, including 15 in 2017 and 7 in nine games last year. He is a mobile, accurate-enough distributor, not someone who wins from the pocket on volume.

The passing efficiency this season comes almost entirely from the short area. On 30 throws at 0-9 air yards he is at +0.389 EPA, 76.7% completions and +8.9 CPOE. Beyond that it thins out quickly. He has gone 2-for-8 on deep shots, and the two completions were both touchdowns, which is a hot finish on a tiny sample rather than a skill. On third down he converted 26.7% with -0.276 EPA per play, facing an average of 7.4 yards to go. The legs still matter: two designed runs went for 44 yards.

The headline number is also padded by when it happened. Trailing by nine or more, mostly the Week 2 blowout at Dallas, he posted +0.604 EPA on 12 plays. In one-score situations, 42 plays, he was at -0.014, roughly league average. Three red-zone touchdowns on four attempts and a pressure-to-sack rate of 10.5% (4th best, against a career habit of 31-42%) are the two figures most likely to drift back toward who he has been. The low sack rate is especially notable because he was pressured on 35.8% of dropbacks, 31st of 32.

The bigger story is availability. He left Week 4 after 16% of snaps with a right MCL sprain, is listed doubtful with a timeline 'to be determined,' and the depth chart already has him back at QB2. Washington is aiming for Jayden Daniels, out with a dislocated left elbow, to practice fully and start against the Giants. If that happens, Mariota goes back to insurance duty, and the knee may limit the mobility that makes him worth playing when he is needed.

strengths.title: Efficient, accurate short passing game
strengths.body: Most of his value comes on quick throws inside 10 air yards, where he completes passes well above expectation and stays on schedule. This fits his career profile, with positive CPOE in 2018 and 2025, so it is the most bankable part of his game. It also travels to any matchup because it does not depend on protection holding up.

strengths.title: Legs as a designed-run threat
strengths.body: He has run for 7.0 yards per carry, and his two designed runs averaged 22 yards. Rushing production is the throughline of his career: he ranked 6th in rushing yards in 2016 and 2022. The open question is whether that survives an MCL sprain in the right knee.

strengths.title: Ball security so far
strengths.body: He has zero interceptions and zero fumbles lost on 57 dropbacks, and the turnover-worthy count is clean too. That is the core requirement for a backup. It is not a career-long trait, though: he threw 7 interceptions in nine games in 2025.

concerns.title: Knee injury and the QB2 role
concerns.body: He is doubtful with a right MCL sprain and an undetermined timeline. Daniels is targeted to start Week 5, and the depth chart lists Mariota as QB2. A knee injury to a QB whose edge is mobility is a particular problem, because the scramble and designed-run value is exactly what a sprain takes away.

concerns.title: Efficiency padded by garbage time
concerns.body: Strip out the plays where Washington trailed by nine or more and the passing is roughly break-even in competitive game states. Third downs were a problem, and the red-zone touchdown rate (three on four attempts) will not hold. The true level is closer to an average backup than his 13th-ranked EPA suggests.

concerns.title: Sack avoidance unlikely to last
concerns.body: He was pressured on more than a third of dropbacks yet turned only 10.5% of pressures into sacks, a sharp break from a career of 31-42% pressure-to-sack rates. On a few dozen dropbacks that looks like variance. Expect more drive-killing sacks if he plays behind a line missing Sam Cosmi.

trend.note: He went from efficient relief in a Dallas blowout, to a full game and a win over Seattle's 3rd-ranked defense, to an injury exit after four throws against Indy. That is too choppy and too small a sample to call a trajectory.

nextGame.headline: Likely sidelined; Daniels expected back against the Giants
nextGame.body:
On paper, the Giants suit his game. They generate the fewest sacks in the league (32nd in sack rate) and the second-fewest QB hits, which would ease a pressure problem he has dealt with all year. Their defense is built to stop the deep ball, 3rd in deep EPA allowed, which matters less for a passer who lives at 0-9 air yards. That short area is where New York is merely middle of the pack (13th).

The catch is that he probably isn't playing. He is doubtful with the MCL sprain, and Washington is targeting a Daniels start. Even if Mariota did play, McLaurin (13 targets, +0.419 EPA per target, his best target by far) is out with a hamstring, and so are starting guard Sam Cosmi and RB Rachaad White. On the Giants' side, DE Chauncey Golston and S Jason Pinnock are questionable, which only thins an already soft pass rush.

keyMatchups.title: Quiet Giants pass rush
keyMatchups.body: New York ranks last in sack rate and 31st in hit rate. That would take pressure off a quarterback pressured on 35.8% of his dropbacks. It is the most favorable part of the matchup for any Washington QB.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots into a strong secondary
keyMatchups.body: The Giants allow few explosive passes and are 3rd in deep EPA allowed. Mariota is 2-for-8 deep this year. Whoever starts should expect to work underneath rather than win over the top.

keyMatchups.title: Missing top target
keyMatchups.body: McLaurin is out, and he produced most of the efficient targets. Without him, the volume shifts to receivers like Diggs and Antonio Williams, who were near zero in EPA per target.

nextGame.watch: Whether Daniels gets through a full practice week. That decides whether Mariota's knee even matters on Sunday.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect Mariota to go back to the clipboard once Daniels is healthy and the knee settles. His fantasy and betting relevance hinges on another Daniels absence. When he does play, the profile is a short-area passer who completes throws and adds yardage with his legs, worth around league-average EPA in competitive games. The 7.8% touchdown rate and the clean sack and interception numbers are the parts that will regress. The interceptions especially have shown up in every extended stint of his career.

The MCL sprain is the wild card. If it lingers, the running that has carried his value for a decade gets muted, and he becomes a fairly ordinary pocket backup. The ranges below are per start, if he is pressed into one.
swingFactors: How the right MCL affects his mobility

bets.reason: He is doubtful with a right MCL sprain and listed as QB2, and Washington is targeting a Daniels start. Any market that assumes Mariota plays meaningful snaps is betting against the team's own stated plan.

The Giants have the league's second-lowest pass rate over expected (-10), which slows the game. Their defense is 3rd against deep passes and 5th in explosive pass rate allowed. Washington's offense is 29th in success rate and loses McLaurin and Cosmi, though Washington games have cleared the total in two of three logged weeks, so this is only a slight edge.

confidence.note: 57 dropbacks across three uneven appearances, an undetermined knee timeline, and a QB2 role tied to Daniels' health.
